story: As an Employee, I want to move my booking to another time or room, so that I keep a room when my plans change.
must_cover: The holder can change the time, the room, or both
Moving is possible only up to the start time; after start the booking cannot be moved
A move re-runs all creation rules: conflict, 30-day horizon, 4-hour maximum, working hours
A conflict on move is rejected with a message naming the conflicting slot and its holder
The holder and attendees receive an updated invite after a move
must_not: An Office Manager or Admin can move another user's booking
Moving after the start time is allowed for any role
An in-app notification is sent
notes: Fully decided in PC 4.2; a good output needs few or no open questions.

story: As an Employee, I want to cancel my own booking, so that the room is free for others.
must_cover: The holder can cancel their own booking up to the start time
After the start time the holder cannot cancel
Cancellation sets the status to cancelled and releases the room immediately
must_not: A cancellation reason is required from the holder
A specific notification to attendees or the holder on self-cancellation is stated as decided
A manual room release action exists
expected_questions: Whether any notification (to the holder or attendees) is sent when the holder cancels their own booking — the PC defines a notice only for Office Manager cancellations
notes: Trap: PC 4.5 defines a cancellation notice only when an Office Manager cancels.

story: As an Office Manager, I want to cancel any booking in my office with a reason, so that I can resolve room conflicts.
must_cover: The Office Manager can cancel any booking in their own office
The Office Manager can cancel before and after the start time
A reason is required to cancel
The holder receives a cancellation notice that includes the reason
Attendees are not notified separately
The room is released immediately
must_not: The Office Manager can cancel bookings in other offices
Attendees receive the cancellation notice
The Office Manager moves the booking instead of cancelling
expected_questions: Reason format or length (free text vs a list) — not stated in the PC; acceptable as TBD or an internal decision
notes: Superseded draft: attendees used to be notified; current PC says holder only.

story: As an Employee, I want to check in to my booking, so that the room stays reserved for me.
must_cover: Check-in opens 10 minutes before the start time
Check-in is done by the holder in the app (who may check in can be implicit in the story statement)
The reminder sent 10 minutes before start carries the check-in link
Check-in changes the status from booked to checked-in
Without check-in by the end of the 15-minute grace period the booking becomes no-show and the room is released (may be a Related story)
must_not: Check-in through a door panel, badge or sensor
Check-in is possible after the booking became no-show
Attendees can check in
expected_questions: Whether the 15-minute grace period should be configurable per office (PC marks the global value as proposed — confirm)
notes: Trap: hardware check-in is Future Phase; check-in after no-show is unreachable.

story: As an Employee, I want to create a weekly recurring booking, so that I don't book the same meeting every week.
must_cover: Recurrence is weekly only
A series has at most 12 occurrences
An occurrence that conflicts with an existing booking is skipped, not the whole series
The holder receives a series-skip notice for a skipped occurrence
The creation rules apply to occurrences (duration, working hours, home office)
must_not: Daily or monthly recurrence
The whole series is rejected on one conflict
A decided answer on how the 30-day horizon applies to a 12-week series
expected_questions: How the 30-day booking horizon applies to a weekly series of up to 12 occurrences (12 weeks exceeds 30 days)
Whether a no-show on one occurrence affects the rest of the series
notes: Key trap: horizon vs series length is not resolved in the PC.

story: As an Office Manager, I want to mark a booking as no-show manually, so that an empty room is released before the grace period ends.
must_cover: The Office Manager can mark a booking in their own office as no-show
Manual no-show is possible before the grace period elapses
Only a booking in status booked (not checked in) can be marked
Marking no-show releases the room
must_not: An Employee can mark no-show
A checked-in booking can be marked no-show
No-show statistics are shown to Employees
expected_questions: Whether the holder is notified when an Office Manager marks their booking as no-show — not defined in the PC
notes: Reachability: no-show applies only to booked; checked-in cannot be marked.

story: As an Admin, I want to deactivate a user, so that people who left the company cannot sign in.
must_cover: Only an Admin deactivates a user (may be implicit in the story statement)
A deactivated user cannot sign in
The user's future bookings are cancelled automatically and the rooms released
Past bookings are retained
Deactivation is reversible; reactivation does not restore cancelled bookings
must_not: Deactivating a Workspace account deactivates the app user
Bookings are deleted
A decided notification to attendees of auto-cancelled bookings
expected_questions: Whether app deactivation should be synced with Workspace account deactivation
Whether holders or attendees of the auto-cancelled future bookings are notified
notes: Sync with Workspace is an explicit open question in the PC.

story: As an Admin, I want to remove the Office Manager role from a user in an office, so that access matches current responsibilities.
must_cover: Only an Admin removes the Office Manager role (may be implicit in the story statement)
The removal is per office
The Admin cannot remove the role from the only remaining Office Manager in an office; another must be assigned first
An Office Manager cannot remove roles, including their own (may be implicit in the role statement)
must_not: The last Office Manager can be removed
Removing the role in one office changes the user's role in another office
expected_questions: Which role the user holds in that office after removal (for example Employee) — not stated in the PC; acceptable as proposed — confirm
notes: Trap: the post-removal role is not defined.
